source.title: Truth or Backpropaganda? An Empirical Investigation of Deep Learning Theory
source.authors: Micah Goldblum; Jonas Geiping; Avi Schwarzschild; Michael Moeller; T. Goldstein

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 models, bearing on whether training reaches near-zero training classification error; it does not test the versions’ specified initialization, width or other mechanisms directly.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy results in Appendix Tables 9–10 bear on V1. Loss and gradient results for constructed local minima in Tables 1 and 5–7 do not report training classification error, so they are not rows. Rank-manipulation results are included only where the tables report training accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study reports near-zero training classification error for convolutional networks on CIFAR-100 under natural, adversarial and rank-manipulated training. These results bear on V1 in additional training settings. Its constructed local minima and NTK measurements do not test the specific mechanisms in V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the local-minima section: poor initialization or hyperparameters can expose suboptimal minima, and the authors attribute ordinary avoidance to refined initializations and stochastic optimizers. The overall conclusion also covers failures of small-norm generalization intuitions, NTK width predictions for ResNets, and a simple association between low rank and robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Reports training accuracy in experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including rank manipulation and adversarial training; it does not reproduce the cited random-initialization, corrupted-label or optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training accuracies vary slightly by dataset, model and training method, but all are at least 99.73%.

fits_no_version.finding: The CIFAR-10 MLP attains 99.97–100.00% training accuracy under natural training and rank fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected networks can attain near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 and retain it after rank manipulation.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical constructions and deliberately unusual initializations produce suboptimal local minima in MLPs and ResNet-18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Realistic neural-network loss landscapes contain suboptimal minima accessible through specially chosen initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing WideResNet width decreases NTK correlation between initialization and the trained model; removing batch normalization or shortcuts changes this trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTK stability with increasing width depends on architecture and the interaction of batch normalization with shortcuts.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixup ResNet-20 has chance-level test accuracy without explicit regularization, while weight decay and norm-bias improve it substantially.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixup model performance under the tested recipe depends strongly on explicit regularization; these test-accuracy results do not measure training speed or stability.

record.problems: The training-accuracy tables do not state initialization or uncertainty. CIFAR-10 training accuracy is reported for an MLP without its size; the CIFAR-100 table reports ResNet-18. Rank-manipulation entries are fine-tuning results, not fresh runs from initialization.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1 and 5–7 report loss and gradient norms for local-minimum experiments rather than training classification accuracy; they were not extracted as V1 rows. Other tables report test accuracy or robustness rather than the training-error behavior in V1.

untested.parts: Random initialization and SGD/Adam are not specified for the linked accuracy results. Corrupted labels, random labels, convolutional-network training accuracy on CIFAR-10, and systematic size, early-stopping or regularization failure comparisons are not tested by these rows.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student width comparison or frequency of spurious minima from standard initialization.
No training-error comparison across depths with and without identity shortcuts; no very deep tanh experiment. Fixup test accuracy does not establish its training-depth or stability claims.
No comparison of activation-matched signal-preserving initializations, learning speed, trainable depth, or orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
No learning-rate sweep relative to a stability threshold or joint loss–curvature trajectory.
No matched comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, or Fixup speed and stability.

missing.what: Six training-accuracy results for ResNet-18 without skip connections: natural 99.96%, RankMax 99.82%, RankMin 99.90%, adversarial 99.92%, RankMaxAdv 99.90%, RankMinAdv 99.91%. All show near-zero training classification error.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Correctly reported MLP accuracies cannot support a claim explicitly scoped to convolutional networks. Constructed bad minima do not challenge standard-initialization convergence, and NTK stability is distinct from optimization stability.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization is not stated; corrupted or random labels, optimizer comparisons, early stopping, and smaller-model or regularization failure conditions are not tested.
